brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: Two full hex bases (0,0) and (1,0) plus a north-half base (0,1), joined with joint bolts on their shared walls.
bin:0,0,0 (3 compartments, open top) and bin:1,0,0 (2 compartments, under the lid). Both are drop-in bins that hang on their rims, so they lift out. Shown holding M3 screws, nuts and standoffs.
drawer:0#0,1#cut sits on the cut face of the half base at (0,1).
handle:1,0,0;top sits on the full cover over cell (1,0). It is off to one side, not at the centre of the build, and nothing here checks how it carries weight or how strong it is.
About 15 parts on three cells in one storey, well under the 30-part limit. Nothing here checks its weight.

finish.summary: Small 3-cell organizer: two bases with removable divided bins, a half base with a drawer, and a lid with a carry handle. The configurator check passed with no mesh clashes.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
